input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: stats.clear() empties the single dict that wrapped_f.statistics holds, and that dict is now reused by every call. Overlapping calls to the same decorated function, whether from threads or from recursion, wipe and overwrite each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: a @retry-decorated function is called concurrently from two threads, or recursively so an inner call starts while an outer call is still running. Previously each call rebound wrapped_f.statistics to its own fresh copy dict. Now the inner or second call clears the shared dict and writes its own values into it, so the outer call's attempt counts and timings are reset or corrupted. The impact is silently wrong retry statistics for the outer call.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label. A single statistics dict is cleared and reused on every call, so concurrent or nested calls to the same decorated function wipe each other's start_time and attempt values. It covers both threads and nested calls, which fits the labeled failure path.
